resumo: Photograph the drawing together with the hand that drew it. Paper yellows, goes missing, ends up as wrapping. The photo stays.

secoes.titulo: The first scribble has a date and it disappears
secoes.texto: Children's drawings pile up fast and go in the bin by sheer volume. The first one, though, is a document: it is the first time she left a mark on the world on purpose. Without a photo and a date, it becomes just another sheet in the stack.

itens: Shoot from above, with the whole sheet in the frame and window light, with no shadow from your hand.
Write the date and the age in the description, not on the paper, so you do not spoil the drawing.
If she can already talk, ask what it is and write the answer down word for word. That sentence is worth more than the drawing.
Photograph her hand holding the crayon too: it gives scale and tells you the stage.

secoes.texto: Thick wax crayons, the stubby ones a closed fist can hold, and large paper, the bigger the better. Small paper turns into frustration; a roll of parcel paper or the back of a poster does the job.
Do not keep them all. Pick one a month, photograph it, and let the rest meet their natural fate. One a month over twelve months is a collection; all of them is a full cupboard nobody opens.
